title: Products Certified under Singapore Green Labelling Scheme and Efforts to Promote Wider Adoption
what_it_is: Products Certified under Singapore Green Labelling Scheme and Efforts to Promote Wider Adoption

sections.label: Green labelling and procurement schemes
sections.summary: The passage lists Singapore's green labelling and certification schemes and the public sector's green procurement requirements under GreenGov.SG.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The Singapore Green Labelling Scheme (SGLS) is administered by the Singapore Environment Council (SEC).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We understand that, to date, SEC has certified over 4,300 products from more than 800 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Others include the National Environment Agency's (NEA's) Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme (MELS), the Public Utilities Board's (PUB's) Mandatory Water Efficiency Labelling Scheme (WELS), the Singapore Food Agency's (SFA's) Farm-To-Table (FTT) Recognition Programme and the Singapore Green Building Council's (SGBC's) Singapore Green Building Product (SGBP) certification scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Under the GreenGov.SG initiative, the public sector has introduced green procurement requirements for nine categories of goods and services, some of which involve the use of green labels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: For example, electrical appliances should meet the specified tick-rating under NEA's MELS, relevant building products are to be accredited with SEC's SGLS or SGBC's SGBP certification scheme, and white printing paper is to be accredited with SEC's Enhanced SGLS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Food and beverage establishments that are accredited by SFA's FTT Recognition Programme can also earn evaluation points when bidding for public sector catering contracts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: These include incorporating reputable green standards, certification schemes or labels where applicable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We will also work with the industry and relevant non-Government organisations to gradually expand the goods and services covered under the public sector's green procurement policies.

sections.label: Incentivising private sector green procurement
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry plans to incentivise private companies to buy sustainability labelled products, citing premium prices and possible grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My one supplementary question is that as Singapore strengthens our move towards more proactive and deliberate efforts to mitigate climate change and further our sustainability efforts, does the Ministry also have plans to further incentivise our local private sector companies to buy from all these sustainability labelled or certified products because some have given feedback that they are a bit more premium priced and add to their operating costs in an already increasing cost environment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: I believe under Enterprise SG, there could be some schemes or grants to help local companies procure more productive or environmentally friendly equipment or products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: I do not have the details now but I believe NEA would also have such grants and schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We will continue to look at what other ways we can nudge the private sector to be greener in their procurement.
